entries.title: Linear
entries.layout: Single-column hero with tight max-width, section breathing room built from consistent 8px grid, full-bleed dark sections alternating with contained content blocks
entries.type: Inter as body/UI, custom display size for hero headline at 72–96px, -0.04em tracking on display, high weight contrast between display (800) and body (400)
entries.color: Near-black background (#0f0f10), pure white primary text, single purple accent (#5E6AD2) used sparingly for interactive states and CTAs only
entries.motion: Subtle scroll-triggered fade-up on section entry at 300ms ease-out, hero gradient orbs drift slowly at 8s loop, no jarring transitions
entries.notes: The grain texture is a CSS noise SVG data-URI overlaid at 3% opacity — creates depth without images. The purple accent never appears in body copy, only in buttons and links. Spacing between sections is 120px desktop / 80px mobile.

entries.title: Vercel
entries.layout: Hero is full-viewport with centered content, persistent horizontal grid lines create depth, below-the-fold sections use a tight 12-column grid
entries.type: Geist as system font (custom variable font), display at 80px weight 800, body at 16px weight 400, strong hierarchy with 3 clear size levels
entries.color: True black background, pure white text, single accent color shifts between pages (green for build, blue for infra). Grid lines at 8% white opacity.
entries.motion: Logo glow pulses on load, deployment status indicators animate in sequence, hero gradient breathes at 12s, scroll-scrubbed feature reveals
entries.notes: The grid lines use CSS background-image with a repeating linear-gradient at 1px — creates a blueprint feel at zero performance cost. The blur-backdrop on the nav only activates on scroll to avoid covering the hero gradient.

entries.title: Stripe
entries.layout: Alternating left/right content blocks with large illustrations, hero uses a gradient mesh that shifts color on scroll, strong asymmetry on feature sections
entries.type: Sohne for display (650 weight, -0.02em tracking), body in system stack, display sizes from 48–72px, generous line-height at 1.1 for headlines
entries.color: White base, the signature Stripe gradient (purple-blue-cyan) used as background mesh not text color, section backgrounds shift hue across the scroll journey
entries.motion: The hero gradient mesh is WebGL-powered, card tilt is CSS perspective on mouse-move, feature reveals use intersection observer with 200ms stagger
entries.notes: The gradient mesh hero is a single canvas element behind all content. Stripe uses a custom WebGL shader for the color shifting — but a CSS conic-gradient approximation at 60% quality costs nothing. The card tilt uses CSS custom properties updated by JS for the perspective calculation.

entries.title: Resn
entries.layout: Full-viewport sections with scroll hijack, work grid uses irregular masonry with hover-expand, no traditional nav — everything is discoverable through interaction
entries.type: Mixed type — each project section uses its own type system. Agency brand uses condensed grotesque at extreme sizes (100vw headlines)
entries.color: White with black type baseline, each project bleeds its own full-color palette into the section, creating jarring but intentional color transitions
entries.motion: Full custom WebGL experience, cursor trails, page transitions are 3D flips, hover states distort images with displacement maps
entries.notes: The displacement map hover effect uses a small greyscale PNG as a WebGL texture and varies the intensity based on mouse velocity — slow hover = subtle, fast swipe = strong distortion. The cursor trail is requestAnimationFrame with lerp interpolation.

entries.title: Lusion
entries.layout: Full-viewport hero with real-time particle simulation, below-fold uses tight single-column editorial layout with large imagery
entries.type: PP Neue Machina (geometric monospace) for brand, system sans for body. Display at extreme contrast — 96px headline next to 14px caption.
entries.color: Black and white primary with the particle simulation providing all color — particles shift from white to chromatic based on interaction, creating emergent color without a fixed palette
entries.motion: The hero is a full physics simulation running in WebGL — particles respond to cursor with spring physics. Scroll scrubs the simulation state. Everything else is minimal.
entries.notes: The spring physics uses a simple Verlet integration — each particle has position, previous-position, and velocity. The cursor creates a repulsion force field. At 60fps with 10k particles this is achievable with instanced mesh in Three.js.

entries.title: Active Theory
entries.layout: Full WebGL scene as background, content layers on top as HTML. Work presented as 3D objects in scene space. Traditional layout completely abandoned.
entries.type: Helvetica Neue at extreme weights — 100 for ambient labels, 700 for headlines. Letter spacing at +0.3em for uppercase labels creates architectural feel.
entries.color: Dark navy (#0a0a14) with electric blue (#00AAFF) as the single accent. All color comes from 3D scene lighting, not surface colors.
entries.motion: Camera moves on scroll through the 3D scene. Mouse parallax on all HTML layers. Work thumbnails are video textures on 3D planes with hover-triggered playback.
entries.notes: The 3D scene uses Three.js PerspectiveCamera with OrbitControls disabled — camera position is driven purely by scroll progress and a bezier path. Video textures on planes: create a <video> element, use it as THREE.VideoTexture, set texture.needsUpdate=true in the render loop.

entries.title: Cactus Club Cafe
entries.layout: Horizontal scroll narrative for hero, then vertical for content. Full-bleed imagery with text layered on top at low opacity. Generous whitespace.
entries.type: Canela (serif) for display at 64px, Aktiv Grotesk for UI. Strong editorial contrast between the serif headline and sans body.
entries.color: Off-white (#f9f6f1) base, dark charcoal (#1a1a1a) text, warm terracotta accent (#c4714e) used for CTAs and hover states.
entries.motion: Horizontal scroll is CSS scroll-snap with JS velocity detection. Image reveals use clip-path animation triggered by intersection observer. Video backgrounds autoplay muted.
entries.notes: The horizontal scroll section uses overscroll-behavior: none on the horizontal container to prevent accidental browser back-navigation. The image reveal clip-path animation: clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) to clip-path: inset(0 0% 0 0) at 600ms cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1).

entries.title: The Last of Us Part II — Ellie model
entries.color: Desaturated skin tones with high-frequency detail in the normal map. Roughness map drives all perceived texture detail — albedo is intentionally flat.
entries.notes: Skin: albedo is 80% desaturated, all perceived color variation comes from the roughness map and a subtle curvature-based SSS gradient. Hair is 200 planes with alpha-tested texture. LOD 0 is 80k tris, LOD 1 is 40k, LOD 2 is 12k. Morph targets for facial animation are stored as separate meshes in the FBX.

entries.title: Arcane — Jinx character
entries.color: Saturated teal hair and jacket with warm skin tones. The stylized look comes from baking a rim-light gradient into the albedo texture rather than relying on real-time lighting.
entries.notes: Stylized PBR: roughness is near-uniform (0.6–0.7) across the character, metallic is used sparingly. The toon outline is a backface-expanded shell with a flat dark material. Skin albedo has a subtle pink-to-orange gradient baked in from the character's warm lighting environment.

entries.title: Cyberpunk 2077 — Yaiba Kusanagi CT-3X motorcycle
entries.color: Matte black primary with chrome trim. Roughness map drives the edge wear — worn edges are roughness 0.2, flat panels are 0.6. Metallic is 1.0 on all chrome surfaces, 0.0 on matte plastics.
entries.notes: Panel lines use a dedicated decal atlas rather than being modeled in — 256x256 decal texture tiled at 2x the base texel density. Edge wear is curvature-driven: high curvature areas get a roughness lerp toward 0.2. Matte black base is albedo (0.03, 0.03, 0.03) linear — not pure black. LOD0: 42k tris, LOD1: 22k, LOD2: 8k.

entries.title: Three.js — GPGPU particle physics scene
entries.motion: GPU-computed particle physics using GPGPU texture ping-pong: position and velocity in float textures, updated each frame in a fragment shader, fed to vertex shader via InstancedMesh.
entries.notes: GPGPU pattern: two RenderTargets, alternate each frame. Velocity shader reads positions, applies forces, writes velocities. Position shader integrates, writes positions. InstancedMesh samples position texture in vertex shader. At 50k instances runs at 60fps on mid-range GPU. Use THREE.DataTexture with FloatType — never IntType.

entries.title: Blender — procedural terrain with geometry nodes
entries.color: Multi-layer material driven by height: rock above 0.7, grass 0.3-0.7, dirt below 0.3. Each layer uses a tiling albedo at 20px/cm, roughness 0.85-0.95.
entries.notes: Geometry nodes: Grid → Subdivide → Noise Displacement (strength 5m, scale 0.15) → second Noise pass (strength 0.5m, scale 2.0) for detail. Material uses ColorRamp on Z position to blend 3 PBR materials by height. Two noise octaves at different scales give natural terrain vs. one. Bake normal map at 4096px before runtime to avoid per-frame displacement cost.

entries.title: Unreal Engine 5 — Nanite-ready asset workflow
entries.notes: Nanite assets need no LOD chain. Still require: clean topology (no N-gons, no non-manifold), UVs for lightmaps (channel 1), separate low-poly collision mesh. For displacement: Nanite Tessellation (UE5.3+) enables true displacement from heightmap at render time. Import scale: 100 UU = 1 meter. Split meshes above 1M tris to avoid cracks.

entries.title: Apple — SF Pro type system
entries.type: SF Pro variable font with optical sizing axes. Display size (36pt+): -0.02em tracking. Text size (11–19pt): 0em. Caption (<11pt): +0.06em. Weight from 200–900.
entries.color: Type is never pure black — uses #1d1d1f (near-black) for body, #86868b for secondary. Never pure white on pure black.
entries.notes: The tracking table is the key insight: tracking gets tighter as size increases, looser as size decreases. At 96px display: -0.04em. At 12px caption: +0.08em. This is the opposite of most systems which apply uniform tracking. The optical size axis on SF Pro adjusts contrast, ink traps, and apertures automatically.

entries.title: Framer Motion — spring examples
entries.motion: Spring: stiffness 300, damping 30 for snappy UI. Stiffness 150, damping 20 for organic. Stagger: 0.05s per item delay. Exit animations are always 60% of entry duration.
entries.notes: The rule of thumb for spring physics: stiffness controls speed, damping controls oscillation. For UI (buttons, modals): high stiffness (300+), high damping (25+) = instant with no bounce. For organic (page elements, cards): lower stiffness (100-200), lower damping (15-20) = visible spring. Exit animations should always be shorter than entrance — 0.6x ratio.

entries.title: Basement Studio
entries.layout: Tight list-based layout rejecting traditional card grids. Work presented as a dense text list with images that reveal on hover via clip-path. No hero in the traditional sense.
entries.type: Monospace (Courier-adjacent) for primary content creates brutalist tension. Large display sizes. No serif.
entries.color: Near-black background, pure white or acid green (#CCFF00) text. The acid green is used for interactive hover states only — never for static content.
entries.motion: Image reveals on text hover: clip-path from inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0) at 400ms cubic-bezier(0.76, 0, 0.24, 1). Marquee is CSS animation, not JS.
entries.notes: The hover image reveal being on text (not the image) is the key technique — it inverts the expected UI pattern and creates surprise. The acid green accent used only on interaction means the page starts monochrome and color only appears when the user acts. Marquee uses animation: marquee 20s linear infinite on a duplicated content block.
